proposal.name: Produce Go test events through a reusable local transport

issue_plan.name: Produce Go test events through a reusable local transport
issue_plan.summary: First add a host-owned local transport with private staging, separate event and diagnostic channels, and bounded process cleanup. Then use it to run a production Go testing lifecycle producer after the existing selection and discovery checks, with default real-Go tests covering outcomes, exact selection, captured flags, diagnostic spoofing and interruption. Together these issues complete #538's producer and local transport; conversion into RepositoryAcceptanceEvidence through RunAcceptance remains the next step of #537. Each issue updates the current-state documentation, and the merger confirms D-0321 and records the transport and producer decisions before dependent work proceeds.

issues.title: Add a reusable host-owned local process transport
issues.body:
This is the first implementation step of #538, which supplies the Go event producer and local transport for step 1 of #537. Build the transport mechanics under internal/plumbing as production Go code, with a working local implementation and default real-process tests. The next issue in this plan adds the Go framework producer on this transport. The transport must be useful without that producer and must not infer test outcomes or implement a substitute reporter.

Contract and operations:

- Define explicit operations for private helper/source staging and reads, subprocess preparation and launch, an independent byte event channel, separate stdout and stderr diagnostics, process wait, bounded drain/shutdown, and release. Preserve literal argument boundaries and the captured owning part's working directory. Keep process exit information and infrastructure errors separate from any future framework terminal records.
- Make the interface transport-neutral: a later prepared-Docker implementation must be able to stage and launch the identical host-owned Go producer and serve the identical future collector without rewriting either. Keep OS process creation and host-to-environment path/endpoint mapping inside the transport implementation. The producer and future collector use its channels and staged-resource contract, without transport-specific rewrites.
- Supply no mandatory new methods on RepositoryAcceptanceAdapter or RepositoryCheckEnvironment. Their existing Select and Run/ReadFile/Close contracts, trusted fake adapters, and Run/Close-only environments continue to work. Use an explicit optional host capability for the new transport; it must not automatically enable an acceptance collector or adapter.
- Define acquisition and ownership precisely, including private directories, files, endpoints, prepared handles and subprocess handles acquired before any preparation or start failure. A handle returned together with an error still belongs to the disposable part environment, which retains responsibility until its shared-lifecycle Close. Failed startup must neither leak resources nor leave an unowned handle. Repeated cleanup must be safe, and release must not discard a previous wait/drain/cleanup error.
- Every validation, read, copy, helper preparation, command and wait inherits the caller's context and remaining allowance. Never create a fresh whole-run or test-phase budget, including for setup after an earlier test. This transport must fit the existing twelve-minute whole run, single ten-minute test phase, shorter caller/preparer limits, and bounded cleanup reserve without introducing a scheduler.
- Close must work with a fresh uncanceled cleanup context after execution cancellation, bounded by the caller and the existing cleanup allowance. Stop and reap real subprocesses, account for child processes that can retain pipes, and bound event/stdout/stderr drains even when an endpoint remains open or a reader/writer stalls. Preserve captured bytes, infrastructure errors and unfinished operations; do not fabricate a terminal test or a successful drain.
- Stage only private regular files with safe ancestors, preserving existing symlink, hard-link, special-file and path confinement refusals. Reuse existing private staging and verbatim acceptance handling where applicable; do not change the original checkout or caller's candidate. The local environment must use an explicitly resolved pinned local Go toolchain and standard library offline, with isolated temporary HOME, build/module caches, GOPATH and temporary storage, no user cache fallback, no installation, downloads, Python or network. Preserve the verified-offline-dependency boundary and do not relax dependency policy to make a local test work. Framework hooks, helper inputs and environment additions are supplied by the host, never candidate configuration.

Default tests and existing contracts:

- Add new Go test files with a distinct transport fixture using small standard-library-only temporary Go modules and actual local Go processes. Exercise literal arguments and working directories, concurrent independent event/stdout/stderr bytes, process exit and launch errors, cancellation, shared deadlines, bounded pipe drains and cleanup, including partially acquired resources and handles returned with errors. Test private staging, unsafe ancestors, candidate/original isolation and isolated caches. Check that no subprocess starts after its context is canceled.
- Opaque byte routing tests may exercise the transport without a framework. They must not manufacture framework lifecycle events, JSON evidence, verdicts or a substitute reporter. All framework outcome tests belong to the next issue and must run the production producer.
- Inspect and preserve the existing process and lifecycle fakes in internal/plumbing/repository_sandbox_accept_test.go, repository_container_accept_test.go, repository_execution_regression_test.go, acceptance_lifecycle_accept_test.go, acceptance_budget_accept_test.go and acceptance_interruption_regression_test.go, including command argument, directory, deadline and cleanup expectations. No existing expectation has been identified as needing a change. If implementation planning finds a necessary existing-test edit, explicitly name that file and explain the necessity in its ratifiable plan before building; do not silently expand scope or weaken the test.
- Keep internal/plumbing/go_selection_accept_test.go, go_discovery_accept_test.go, go_discovery_regression_test.go and go_lifecycle_accept_test.go unchanged. In particular goEnvironment527.Run remains limited to go list/env/version and go test -c and continues refusing test execution; its no-collector controls remain. Do not turn a discovery-only fixture into the runtime transport.
- Preserve acceptance_evidence_accept_test.go, acceptance_foundation_regression_test.go, native_execution_accept_test.go, native_identity_accept_test.go, other native hash/lock regressions and built-in sandbox coverage. Do not add a mandatory transport or collector capability to the existing trusted fake adapters.

Documentation and scope:
Update SPEC.md and docs/factory.md for the implemented local transport and its ownership/context contract, and update README.md's adapter-status sentence to distinguish the available transport from the still-pending producer and evidence conversion. Keep the README at most 400 lines and link to docs/factory.md for details. New or changed SPEC bullets cite recorded decisions; do not claim subsequent steps have shipped. Configured planning admission, default and candidate-controlled adapter registration, external plumbing and production pytest/Vitest/Jest stay disabled. Legacy Go execution, hashes and locks stay unchanged without inferred metadata or migration. This issue implements no RepositoryAcceptanceEvidence conversion, prepared-Docker runtime transport or broader shared integration from step 2 of #536.

Foundations: D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301, D-0305, D-0311 (#484), D-0314 (#503), D-0316 (#515) and D-0321 (#527). D-0321 is already recorded at decisions/journal/D-0321.jsonl; do not invent a replacement ID. Merger work: confirm that decision and record the new transport decision before the dependent producer issue proceeds. Plumbing builds cannot modify decisions/ or .github/. Unavailable Docker/network checks and decision recording alone do not require repair; default real-Go tests are required, and affected opt-in real Python/TLAPS suites remain required in pull-request CI.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Produce authentic Go testing events over the local transport
issues.body:
Complete #538 by implementing a working host-owned Go testing lifecycle producer over the production local transport delivered by the preceding issue in this plan. This is still step 1 of #537: expose the authentic bound stream, diagnostics and process/infrastructure results, but leave validation and conversion of the stream into RepositoryAcceptanceEvidence through RunAcceptance to #537's separately planned next step. Do not substitute synthetic records for the producer.

Production framework boundary:

- Implement the producer, helper/framework hook, preparation and event protocol as production Go code under internal/plumbing, using only the pinned local Go toolchain and standard library offline. No Python, installation, downloads, network, user caches or test-owned event producer. Use the preceding issue's transport operations; do not embed local process ownership into the producer. A future prepared-Docker transport must run this identical producer and the identical future collector.
- Obtain starts and terminal results directly from the Go testing lifecycle through the event channel independent of BOTH workload stdout and stderr. Do not parse go test output, test2json output, lifecycle-looking text or framing-looking diagnostics into event records. Compilation, process exits, synthetic failure records and runner markers cannot stand in for a framework terminal event.
- Implement actual lifecycle hooks rather than wrapping a test function and guessing its verdict. Preserve Go's TestMain, initialization, t.Run nesting, parallel children, cleanup, skip, assertion failure and panic behavior. Keep instrumentation host-owned and private, with acceptance bytes, ordinary production sources, dependencies, build constraints and ordinary/external test packages preserved. Any toolchain-specific instrumentation must check that it can safely apply to the pinned toolchain and report preparation failure rather than fall back to textual inference.
- Preserve exact runtime test and parent names, ordered starts and terminal events, and the lifecycle information needed to validate nested and parallel completion later. Parallel descendants must finish as Go specifies before their parent is reported complete. Do not equate discovery of a parent with execution of an exact selected child. Keep framework explanations/log context for actual pass, failure and skip; retain panic explanations. Distinguish a genuine assertion failure or panic with framework failure completion from an abrupt exit with no terminal events.
- Define the stream boundary so the host's fresh InvocationID, full (part, framework, file, selector) identity, verbatim acceptance Source, SourceDigest and captured ExecutionDigest remain bound throughout preparation and production. Use the import path returned by production discovery, retaining the selected runtime name separately from the requested selector. Candidate configuration, diagnostic claims, an identical display label, another file/package/module/part and a top-level declaration cannot establish that the requested runtime case ran. Preserve ordered stream bytes/records and all available diagnostics for the later collector, including on incomplete execution.

Selection, discovery and execution:

- Reuse GoRepositoryAcceptanceAdapter.Select and Discover in go_acceptance.go and go_discovery.go, and the binding/private-staging foundations in repository_acceptance.go. Add no alternate selection, package-loading, declaration or ownership policy. Provide a production entry path that validates the captured selection before preparation and, after private part preparation, performs actual package loading, verbatim-source/inclusion/declaration checks and successful compilation before invoking the producer. No wrong-file, excluded-file, duplicate-declaration, wrong-module, malformed-source, unresolved-dependency or other discovery failure may invoke it.
- Execute each selector separately from its captured owning part directory with the safely narrowed test_one argument array, ordinary local package imports and local module ownership intact. Before discovery, stage the verbatim pinned bytes privately even when the caller's candidate has equivalent normalized line endings. Never write the original checkout or candidate. Preserve existing verified offline dependencies and safe regular-file/ancestor checks.
- Preserve docs/factory.md's full command grammar: literal go test; exactly one separate or equal-form -run whose entire value is {test} or ^{test}$; omitted scope or exactly one clean inclusive ., ./dir, ./... or ./dir/... scope. Narrow only to the acceptance file's package, never widen, cross module boundaries or enter Go-skipped recursive directories. Independently regexp-escape and anchor every slash-separated selector component; punctuation and shell-looking names are literal arguments.
- Preserve both value spellings, argument order, boundaries and semantics of -tags; nonnegative -timeout including 0; one positive value for each of -parallel, -p and -cpu; -shuffle off/on or a signed integer seed; -mod readonly/vendor; -count exactly 1, adding it when absent; and bare or =true/=false -short, -v, -race and -trimpath. Host instrumentation may add only host-owned mechanics without dropping, overriding or refusing supported captured flags. In particular it must work independently of verbosity, retain explicit false booleans, and preserve Go's own errors for unsupported toolchain/environment combinations rather than quietly changing requested race or build behavior.
- Continue refusing repeated/conflicting or unsupported flags, wrappers, executable paths, opaque commands, file/import-path/multiple scopes and every other unsupported form before preparation. Candidate-specified hooks, overlays, environment overrides and transport registration must not gain authority. Host-only instrumentation does not make such captured commands admissible.

Time and ownership:
Every validation, read, real package load, compilation, helper preparation and runtime process inherits the caller's context and remaining allowance through the preceding transport. Reuse the existing twelve-minute run and single ten-minute test phase, including shorter caller/preparer limits; do not add a scheduler or refresh either budget. The disposable part environment owns helpers, endpoints and partial-start resources until shared-lifecycle Close, including a handle returned alongside an error. Use bounded uncanceled cleanup after cancellation, stop and reap real children, bound pipe drains, and retain infrastructure/cleanup errors and incomplete lifecycle. No cancellation, compile error, wait result, cleanup failure or truncated stream may invent framework completion. Keep these capabilities optional so existing Run/ReadFile/Close-only environments and trusted fake adapters acquire no mandatory start or collector method.

Required default Go tests:
Add a separate runtime process fixture in new Go test files. It may launch actual processes and own private temporary storage, but must exercise production Select, Discover, the producer and the transport with small standard-library-only temporary modules and isolated temporary caches. Never manufacture framework events, JSON evidence or verdicts. Outcome tests require actual loading, compilation and execution without Docker, network or opt-in flags. The following coverage is part of this issue, not an unplanned follow-up:

1. Use the SAME unchanged acceptance source and selector to obtain a real assertion-failure terminal event against a base production file, then a real pass after changing only that production file. Check bound source/digests, actual import path, fresh InvocationIDs and original/candidate immutability.
2. Cover top-level tests; exact nested cases with regexp punctuation and shell-looking names; nested parallel children with ordered parent/child completion; prefix, sibling and parameter-case neighbors that must not execute; and absent children that leave the discovered parent distinguishable from the missing target. Check repeated names across packages, separate modules and nested parts, an external test package, ordinary local production imports, included/excluded build tags and module boundaries. Check wrong-file/duplicate/excluded/wrong-module/discovery/compile refusals stop before producer launch, and unsupported commands stop before any preparation.
3. Exercise supported captured flags through actual executions AND literal argument observations, covering separate and equals values, argument ordering and boundaries, bare/true/false booleans, timeout 0, count 1 and insertion when absent, shuffle off/on/signed seed, tags, parallelism, package build parallelism, CPU value, readonly/vendor, verbosity, short, race and trimpath. Use uninstrumented real-Go controls where needed to verify semantics and Go's own treatment of the flags, including toolchain/environment errors; never mask a flag error or drop a supported flag to make instrumentation pass. Tests must detect changed policy, not merely assert the parser's output.
4. Observe authentic pass, fail and skip with explanations, including behavior when verbosity is false. Exercise zero-test execution and absent selectors without manufacturing a requested terminal result; TestMain exiting before m.Run; initialization and TestMain effects; nonzero abrupt exits before a test and during a started test; panic with actual framework failure completion; and cancellation of a genuinely running process. Check no-start versus started-but-unfinished separately. Cover TestMain and cleanup behavior against ordinary Go execution, including nested/parallel failure propagation.
5. Print misleading PASS/FAIL, Go lifecycle lines, test2json JSON, runner records, framing-looking bytes and complete binding-looking records to BOTH stdout and stderr during initialization, TestMain and tests. Cover real pass with false failure, real failure with false success, and incomplete execution with both claims. Compare with otherwise equivalent uncorrupted controls. Assert only the independent lifecycle channel supplies events, diagnostic bytes remain inspectable in their proper channels, and spoofed binding-looking diagnostics cannot replace the host binding. Tests must fail if a text/JSON parser or fixture-generated reporter substitutes for the production hook. Evidence-conversion extensions of these cases remain #537's next step.
6. Exercise cancellation and inherited deadlines during source validation/reads, preparation, real package loading, compilation, helper work and execution. Bound actual process interruption and pipe draining; exercise partial prepare/start failure and nonnil handles returned with errors, successful and failed cleanup with uncanceled bounded contexts, and repeated release. Retain captured events/diagnostics, infrastructure errors and unfinished work without claiming completion. Do not only test an already-canceled context or a fake wait.

Compatibility:
Keep internal/plumbing/go_selection_accept_test.go, go_discovery_accept_test.go, go_discovery_regression_test.go and go_lifecycle_accept_test.go unchanged. goEnvironment527.Run must still allow only go list/env/version and go test -c, refuse test execution and retain its no-collector controls. The trusted go_discovery_regression_test.go collector continues testing discovery-to-collector binding only; it is never evidence of authentic runtime production. Add the runtime fixture separately rather than broadening these fixtures.

Preserve acceptance_lifecycle_accept_test.go, acceptance_evidence_accept_test.go, acceptance_budget_accept_test.go, acceptance_foundation_regression_test.go, acceptance_interruption_regression_test.go, native_execution_accept_test.go, native_identity_accept_test.go, all other native hash/lock regressions and built-in sandbox coverage. No existing test or command expectation has been identified as needing weakening. If later planning finds a necessary edit to another existing test, explicitly name that file and justify the necessity in the ratifiable implementation plan before building. Preserve the optional adapter/environment boundaries and the preceding issue's transport tests.

Documentation and non-goals:
Update SPEC.md, docs/factory.md and README.md's adapter-status sentence to describe the working production Go event producer and local transport accurately. Explain the independent framework stream, binding, unchanged full command grammar, resource ownership and remaining evidence conversion in docs/factory.md. Keep the README at most 400 lines and link to that page. Every new or changed SPEC bullet cites recorded decisions; no placeholder decision IDs. Do not describe raw event production as completed native acceptance. Configured planning admission, default and candidate-controlled adapter registration, external plumbing and production pytest/Vitest/Jest remain disabled. Preserve legacy Go execution, hashes and locks without inferred metadata or migration. Do not implement RepositoryAcceptanceEvidence conversion/RunAcceptance collection, compiler-failure qualification, the broader shared integration already assigned to step 2 of #536, or the prepared-Docker runtime transport assigned to the separate second step of #534.

Foundations: D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301, D-0305, D-0311 (#484), D-0314 (#503), D-0316 (#515), D-0321 (#527) and the preceding issue's recorded transport decision. D-0321 already exists at decisions/journal/D-0321.jsonl; do not invent a replacement ID. Merger work: confirm D-0321 and record the new producer/transport decision before #537's evidence-conversion step proceeds. Plumbing builds cannot modify decisions/ or .github/. Genuinely unavailable Docker/network checks and decision recording alone do not require repair; default real-Go tests are required, and affected opt-in real Python/TLAPS suites remain required in pull-request CI.

Kind: plumbing
